issues.failure_explanation: The claim that the trajectory stays in the interior of the reparametrized domain for all times is false. Counterexample: sigma_out = Id, L(u,v) = (u-v)^2, A = [1], y = -1, rho_rp(z) = |z|^(2/p) with p in (1,2) (so D = D_rp = [0,infty), satisfying A2), w-prod_0 = alpha > 0. The flow w' = -grad L(w) with L(w) = (|w|^(2/p)+1)^2 satisfies d/dt w^(2-2/p) = -(8(p-1)/p^2)(|w|^(2/p)+1) <= -(8(p-1)/p^2) < 0 for w > 0, so w reaches 0 at a finite time t* and stays there; hence w-prod(t*) = 0, a boundary point of [0,infty), contradicting (i). The proof is invalid: it infers local Lipschitz continuity from mere continuity, and in w-prod coordinates the vector field behaves like w-prod^(2-p) near the boundary, which is not Lipschitz for p > 1, so the Picard-Lindelof uniqueness argument at the boundary fails exactly in the regime where finite-time boundary contact occurs.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair preserves the statement: one must either add a hypothesis excluding finite-time boundary contact (e.g., z -> h'(z)^(-1) locally Lipschitz on the closed domain, which holds for sinh, tanh and |z|^(2/p) only for p <= 1), losing the advertised p in (1,2) regime of the polynomial corollaries, or develop a boundary-limit KKT argument not present in the source. At minimum, a repair must restrict Theorem 2.1(i) and re-derive the interior-based conservation identity for any regime in which boundary contact can occur.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised guarantee of a well-behaved interior trajectory fails for reparametrizations whose (h')^(-1) vanishes slower than linearly at the boundary, notably rho_rp(z) = |z|^(2/p) with p in (1,2). All arguments that derive the mirror-flow conservation calculus from Theorem 2.1(i) — Theorem 2.1(ii) via Lemma theorem:vector_general, Lemma lem:decay, Theorem thm:Convergence, and the polynomial corollaries — are unsupported in that regime.
issues.title: Theorem 2.1(i): reparametrized flow can hit the domain boundary in finite time
issues.why_classification: The statement is false in the regime p in (1,2) on which the paper's own polynomial corollaries rely; the only verifiable repair excludes that advertised regime (half of the l1-to-l2 interpolation), and no boundary-handling argument exists in the source.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where the penultimate step follows from the Polyak-Lojasiewicz inequality together with Remark~\ref{rem:PL} (ii), and the last equality uses that $\A\widetilde\z_0 = \y$.

issues.failure_explanation: The remark claims f = g composed with A inherits the PL inequality with constant sigma_min(A)^2 mu, where sigma_min is the smallest non-zero singular value. This requires A to have full row rank: in general |A^T v| >= sigma_min(A)|v| fails for v in ker(A^T), so gradient components of g orthogonal to the range of A are invisible to the gradient of f. Counterexample with convex C^1 g: g(u) = (1/2)dist(u,C)^2 for a half-space C with unit normal at angle theta satisfies PL with mu = 1 (since |grad g|^2 = 2g); for A = (1,0)^T (single non-zero singular value 1), f(z) = g(z,0) = (1/2)(z cos(theta) - b)_+^2 has best PL constant cos^2(theta) < 1. Consequently the explicit exponential rate in Theorem thm:Convergence(ii), whose proof applies the remark to L(.,y), is false for row-rank-deficient A (the true rate involves the restricted PL constant, which can be strictly smaller; with non-convex PL losses the restricted loss can even have plateaus and the flow can stall).

Counterexample (for the trigonometric version covered by the same defect): M = N = 2, A = I, y = (1,0), sigma_out = Id, rho_rp = sinh, w-prod_0 = alpha*1 small, L(u,v) = phi_1(u_1-v_1) + phi_2(u_2-v_2) with phi_i smooth, nonnegative, zero only at 0, and phi_1 decreasing on (-3,-1) with a spurious local minimum.
